chunks: And the Shaykh — may Allah support him — informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from 'Uthman, from Sama'ah, from Abu Basir, who said: I heard him say:

"When a man vomits while he is in a state of taharah (ritual purity), let him rinse his mouth. And when he has a nosebleed while he is in a state of wudu, let him wash his nose. For that is sufficient for him, and he does not repeat his wudu."
And even if it were conceded that in the Sharia it admits of nothing but the specific wudu, we would interpret it as recommended (mustahabb) on account of the reports we are about to mention.

Among them is what the Shaykh — may Allah, the Exalted, support him — informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Yahya and Ahmad ibn Idris jointly, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him). Jabir said: I heard him say:
"If I had a nosebleed amounting to a dawraq's worth, I would not do more than wiping the blood from me and praying."

key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَابِ: recommended act (mustahabb) — an act whose performance is rewarded but whose omission is not punished
key_terms.دَوْرَقًا: a dawraq — a large earthenware vessel used as a unit of liquid measure (Persian loanword)

ai.seo_question: Does nosebleed or vomiting invalidate wudu according to Shia hadith in Tahdhib al-Ahkam?
ai.summary: This passage from Tahdhib al-Ahkam presents two narrations on the ruling of nosebleed and vomiting with respect to wudu. The first, transmitted via Abu Basir, holds that these events do not nullify wudu — rinsing the mouth after vomiting and washing the nose after a nosebleed are sufficient. The compiler then cites a second report from Imam al-Baqir (AS) via Jabir, in which the Imam declares that even a copious nosebleed amounting to a dawraq's measure would not lead him to do more than wipe the blood and pray.
